Simulation of the alert complexity estimators

Source: R/cxsim.R
cxsim.Rd

Draws person-year tables from the model of Ruhela (2026) and reports the bias, spread and interval coverage of the estimators of cxvol(). Each table has n person-years in ncl regional clusters with normal intercepts (standard deviation sdcl), an age group (three levels) and a gender, a treatment drawn from a logistic model in which the covariates and the cluster raise the chance of a complex profile, and a negative binomial count (dispersion theta) whose log mean is b0 + beta * cx plus the covariates and the cluster. With conf the person-year also has an unobserved trait that raises both the chance of treatment and the count (by conf on the logit and on the log mean): ignorability given the observed covariates then fails.

Usage

cxsim(
  reps = 200,
  n = 2000,
  beta = log(1.3),
  ncl = 24,
  sdcl = 1,
  theta = 2,
  b0 = -2.5,
  conf = 0,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

reps

The replicates: a whole number from 1.

n

The person-years of each table: a whole number from 50.

beta

The log rate ratio of cx.

ncl, sdcl

The clusters and the standard deviation of their intercepts.

theta

The negative binomial dispersion.

b0

The intercept of the log mean.

conf

0, or the effect of the unobserved trait.

seed

The seed of the whole run, set once before the first table is drawn: one whole number. The session's own random stream is left as it was.

Value

An object of class cxsim, a list: res, one row per estimator (est, bias, sd, rmse, cover, ok the replicates fitted); draws, every replicate's estimates; and the settings.

Details

The estimators: crude, the Poisson rate ratio of cx alone; mixed, cntmix() on the full table with the covariates (log rate ratio, Wald interval); matched, cntmix() on the frame matched as in cxvol(). The target is beta, the log rate ratio given the covariates and the cluster, which the model holds constant (proof() names the log-link identity). Results are bias (mean estimate less beta), sd, rmse, and cover, the share of 95% intervals holding beta (NA for crude, which reports no interval). Each replicate is a fresh table from seed; a fit that fails is left out and counted.

Examples

cxsim(reps = 1, n = 100, ncl = 5, b0 = 0, seed = 1)
#> cxsim: 1 tables of 100 person-years, log rate ratio 0.2624
#>      est   bias sd   rmse cover ok
#>    crude 0.4090 NA 0.4090    NA  1
#>    mixed 0.1381 NA 0.1381     1  1
#>  matched 0.0113 NA 0.0113     1  1
